title: Make role prompts carry a request's real goal through to the verdict
summary: Edit the reader, producer and verifier prompts so the reader names the audience, writes an outcome criterion and reads current output; the producer treats criteria as a floor; and the verifier judges output as its audience would. In judge(), a non-empty request_reading_mismatch becomes a Major finding that blocks a pass. Raise the reader budget just enough for the new text and record why.

defaults_applied.how: A reading mismatch counts as major through code in judge(), not through prompt prose alone.
Unit tests for the new judge() behavior. The budgets test passes at the new budget. Clippy clean.
The fix covers all three roles where the goal was lost (reader, producer, verifier), not only the reading.
The new budget is a measured token count, and the recorded reason cites the budgets test output.
The decision record and changelog explain the change for an outside reader.
One focused change to the prompts, the verdict logic and the budget, with no broader refactor.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: 'Counts as major in code' means a mechanism in judge() (athena-core verify.rs) as well as prompt text, per the mechanism default. The prompt line alone would be prose-only.

The reader's budget rises only as far as the added rules need. I estimate roughly 1,950 to 2,100 tokens, to be measured. Other role budgets stay unchanged unless the producer or verifier additions overflow them, in which case they rise too, with reasons recorded.
The contract stays untouched, and no schema change is needed because request_reading_mismatch already exists in the verifier output.
The study capability's prompt files, if separate, are out of scope. Only the three role prompts in crates/athena-context/prompts change.

acceptance_criteria.text: reader.md tells the reader to name the request's audience (who will use or judge the result) in the summary or assumptions.
reader.md requires at least one acceptance criterion written as an outcome that the named audience can check. Presence checks (a section or file exists) alone do not satisfy it.
reader.md forbids putting the request's own stated goal in out_of_scope, and tells the reader to read the current output (page, file, behavior) the request is about before planning a change to it.

producer.md treats the acceptance criteria as a floor: it tells the producer to serve the request's goal, and not stop at the literal criteria or change only what they need. It keeps the small-change discipline and the instruction to follow conventions.

verifier.md tells the verifier to judge user-facing output as its intended audience would, and to rate a request-reading mismatch as at least major. It must not downgrade a gap in the request's goal to minor because the criteria passed.

In crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs, judge() adds a Major finding and a reason when the verifier output has a non-empty request_reading_mismatch, so the verdict is not pass. Unit tests cover a mismatch present (not pass) and absent or blank (unchanged). Run: cargo test -p athena-core verify

The reader budget in BudgetSet::Reader is raised only as far as the new reader text needs, and no further. The budgets test passes at the new value. Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test budgets

docs/decisions.md records the new reader budget, the measured token count and the reason: the new rules cannot be paid for by removals. CHANGELOG.md notes the change. Other documents that state 1,800 are updated.
The workspace stays clean and tested. Run: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, cargo test

out_of_scope: Fixing the firstmate explainer page from job 20261014-154909-f4bt.
Changing the contract prompt or the defaults list.
Changing the verifier output schema or record schemas.
Raising the producer or verifier budgets beyond what the new text needs.
departures: This touches three prompts, a code path with new tests, and a budget constant with documentation. It is larger than the typical job in the reference. The producer must fit tight token budgets, and past reader-budget retries needed several attempts, so I raise cost and time and lower the pass probability slightly.
